articles.title: Check Your NGINX HTTP/2 Config Before Attackers Do
articles.excerpt: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, were disclosed on November 18. Both require HTTP/2 to be enabled, and neither needs authent…
articles.body: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, were disclosed on November 18. Both require HTTP/2 to be enabled, and neither needs authentication. An attacker who reaches the port can potentially run code on the server itself. Your application code can be flawless and it will not matter. The bug lives in the web server in front of it. By the end of this article you will know how to inventory your NGINX deployments for HTTP/2, decide between patching and disabling HTTP/2, and set up detection for exploitation attempts. What the bugs actually are CVE-2026-123633 is a use-after-free in the HTTP/2 request handling path.
articles.author: RobustTrueTry

articles.title: Embeddings and vector databases, explained with one small piece of arithmetic
articles.excerpt: A customer asks a support agent, "How do I get my money back?" The right page is titled "Refund and cancellation terms". The agent's search says "0 results". Keyword search needs the same letters, and…
articles.body: A customer asks a support agent, "How do I get my money back?" The right page is titled "Refund and cancellation terms". The agent's search says "0 results". Keyword search needs the same letters, and these two texts share no words. Embeddings fix this. Here is the idea in plain language, with one worked example using made-up numbers. The idea in three lines An embedding turns a sentence into a short list of numbers, like an address on a map. Sentences with similar meaning get nearby addresses, even with no shared words. A vector database stores the addresses and quickly finds the nearest ones. Picture a city. Cafes cluster in one district and banks in another. Here the places are sentences and the districts are topics. Nobody types in a list of synonyms.

articles.body: SearchBlox Admin APIs and Consoles Share One High-Value Boundary SearchBlox combines a search service with an administrative console and a REST API. The search results may be intentionally public. The administrator controls collections, documents, users, licensing, backups, clustering, and security settings. Those roles should not share the same network treatment merely because they run on the same server. The SearchBlox API documentation describes the API under port 8443 and /api , with interactive documentation and authentication using administrator credentials or an apikey . The administrative feature documentation adds a web console, an API explorer, and roles including Super Admin and Manager. The documentation also describes a unique SB-PKEY private key for API requests.

articles.body: Disclosure: CheapClankers maintains the tool described here and operates a paid developer API service. This article was prepared with AI. The generated Node.js and Python programs were tested against a local mock API; those checks do not establish production model availability. When switching an OpenAI SDK to another compatible endpoint, there are two separate questions: Did the client construct the intended HTTP request? Does the selected model support that request for this key, right now? A successful answer to the first question does not establish the second. To make the first request easier to inspect, we published a small browser-only API setup builder . It generates Node.js, Python and Bash/cURL examples from an API base URL, optional model ID and output limit.

articles.title: Zero-Server AI: Running LLMs and Vector Search Inside the Browser with WebGPU
articles.excerpt: Executive Summary (Quick Answer): Zero-server AI shifts neural inference, semantic embeddings, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) out of centralized GPU clusters and directly onto the user's bro…
articles.body: Executive Summary (Quick Answer): Zero-server AI shifts neural inference, semantic embeddings, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) out of centralized GPU clusters and directly onto the user's browser tab. Powered by the W3C WebGPU Specification , compiled WebGPU engines like mlc-ai/web-llm and huggingface/transformers.js achieve 40x to 100x speedups over legacy WebAssembly CPU fallbacks, reaching roughly 90 tokens per second on Apple Silicon for 4-bit quantized 3B models and sub-5ms latency for local embeddings. Combined with persistent binary caching in the Origin Private File System (OPFS) and native desktop fallbacks via tauri-apps/tauri and lancedb/lancedb , engineering teams can ship private, offline-capable AI products with zero recurring per-token inference bills.

articles.title: Label Created Is Not Shipped: How Fake Tracking Quietly Buys Suppliers Two Weeks
articles.excerpt: Your dashboard says shipped. The carrier has never seen the parcel. The customer pastes the tracking number into the carrier's own site, because your store's tracking page has said the same thing for…
articles.body: Your dashboard says shipped. The carrier has never seen the parcel. The customer pastes the tracking number into the carrier's own site, because your store's tracking page has said the same thing for nine days: "Label created." She writes to you — reasonably — that she thinks the number is fake. You write to the supplier. The supplier writes back that the parcel is "in transit, please wait." Three parties, three different stories, and only one verifiable fact: no carrier has ever scanned the box. This is the most common tracking failure in dropshipping, and it is not always fraud. A tracking number is created when a label is generated, which can happen days before a parcel is packed, handed over, or even exists.

articles.title: Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
articles.excerpt: The answer to one of Earth's greatest geological mysteries may lie deep beneath our feet.
articles.body: More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged.

articles.title: ULA traces Vulcan Centaur rocket failure to 'inadequate fuel supply' to 1st-stage engines
articles.excerpt: United Launch Alliance has traced the Nov. 15 failure of its Vulcan Centaur rocket to an inadequate supply of propellant to the vehicle's first-stage engines.
articles.body: United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend. That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further. "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18). This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4.
